findings.title: In a cloud session the only canvas is the Artifact, and its fallback for missing views sends the person in a loop
findings.claim: When localhost can't be reached (a cloud session, Claude Code on the web or on a phone, a container host), the Artifact is the only canvas there is. That Artifact can't show other lenses, PathView, Anatomy, the impact heat ramp, evidence text or diff hunks. Its fallback empty state tells the person to run /room open, but on exactly those hosts /room open returns opened:false and points back to /room share. The person ends up on a circular dead end, and on that surface Lenses (one of R14's five ideas), R2's 'how does A reach B' with evidence, and R3 breakdowns are missing.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1316 (also DR-56): on the Artifact, 'PathView, Anatomy, the impact heat ramp, evidence text, diff hunks, other lenses and intent next render ... "Needs your computer: open this view there with /room open"', and its button is 'Back to the map'. architecture.md:1198 (also DR-29 round 2): `open` 'Where no browser can be seen (... a container host ...) opens nothing and returns opened:false with an empty state whose next action is /room share'. architecture.md:503 names cloud sessions (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE) as a supported temporary host. mod-spike.md: 'A cloud session with no app attached ... no-surface'. contracts.md Snapshot: `maps: every level for the default lenses`. KICKOFF R13: the canvas is 'beautiful and fast on desktop and phone ... also published as a Claude Artifact for when localhost isn't reachable'. R14 lists Lenses as a core idea. Principle 1: 'Never show a blank state' and 'understanding and control at a fraction of the effort'.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner works in a cloud Claude Code session (the environment KICKOFF describes) and presses e or types /room open. The result is opened:false with next /room share. They share, open the Artifact on their phone and tap the lens swatch to see the release lens, or tap a lifted edge to see why A depends on B. The page says 'Needs your computer: open this view there with /room open'. Back in the session, /room open again says /room share. No surface they can reach ever shows a non-default lens, a path with its evidence, or a breakdown.
findings.proposed_fix: (1) Make the unavailable state depend on the host. Record in the snapshot whether the sharing host can open a browser (opened:false or a temporary host). If it can't, the next action is Send to Claude with a prefilled ask (or 'Ask in your session: /room ask path A B'), never /room open. (2) Grow the snapshot so it covers the five concepts: lifted edges for every lens at every level (counts plus evidence path and line, no contains), measured against the 1 MB fixture budget in WS8. (3) Compute PathView and the impact radius client-side as pure functions in @planroom/ui over the snapshot graph, checked against the Rust `ask path` and `ask impact` goldens, the same way the machine step-through already works. (4) Include the Breakdowns of scanned artifacts and the hunks of the top pending diffs within a byte cap. Add an artifact.spec.ts case: a snapshot made with opened:false never shows /room open.

findings.title: Cycling lenses and projects one key at a time breaks the two-keystroke rule
findings.claim: The pane's only lens control is `l`, 'next lens', and its only project control is `p`, 'next project'. v0.1 ships 10 lenses (11 with S10's toy pack) and S8 needs at least two projects. Reaching a given lens can take up to 9 presses. 'Show the observability lens' or 'switch to project B' is an action, and there's no two-key route to either.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1255: 'z up a level, x down, l next lens, p next project'. architecture.md:716-727 list 10 lenses: runtime, flow, dependencies, history, deployment, release, observability, plan, anatomy, machines. KICKOFF S9: 'Every action is at most two keystrokes from pane focus'. The feature_list S9 assert ('at most two real key presses from pane focus') covers only the scripted flows, and the key map has no lens or project list.
findings.failure_scenario: In the live S9 evidence run, the person answers S2's 'How does observability work here?' from the pane: /room, then `l` six times to get from runtime to observability. For machines it's nine presses. keys.test.tsx::main_flows_within_two_keys either fails on a lens switch or leaves lens switching out of the scripted flows, and the KICKOFF bar is quietly not met.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `l` and `p` open the lens list and the project list in the list area, ranked with the current default first. Each entry gets a row key, so any lens or project is `l` plus its row key (two keys). Pressing `l` twice can keep the 'next' behavior. Add lens and project switching to the scripted flows in main_flows_within_two_keys, with the target as the last row.

findings.title: Actions on rows behind a list key, and stage runs through their cost card, take three or four keys
findings.claim: 'Acting on any visible row takes at most two keys' counts only rows that are already on screen. Many main-flow targets first need a list-opening key (i, f, w, t, and in the compact layout d), then a row key, then the action key. A plan-stage run also has to clear its cost card. So R5's stage jumps, drift actions, presence and claims, the remote list (Pair, sync), and diffs in the compact layout all take three or more keys from pane focus. The S9 assert is scoped to 'any visible row', so it can pass while KICKOFF's bar isn't met.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1257: '`i` intent: the stages, then lint findings, as list rows; Enter on a stage runs it'. architecture.md:1262: the list area is 'the list the last key opened'. architecture.md:1268: 'So acting on any visible row takes at most two keys'. architecture.md:1269: 'drafting a plan stage, shows ... its card in the pane, where confirming takes a second, deliberate key'. DR-54 round 2: 'Enter on a stage row under i runs that stage through its cost card'. architecture.md:1266: in the compact layout 'Diffs, drift, who and the mini-map move behind their keys (d, f, w, m), each shown in place of the list'. feature_list S9 assert: 'Enter on a stage row under i runs intent next --stage S through its cost card, within two keys from pane focus' and 'at most two real key presses from pane focus, on any visible row'. KICKOFF S9 and R5 ('The person can jump between stages').
findings.failure_scenario: S3 from the pane: running the outcome stage is `i` (open stages), Enter (the stage ranked first), then the cost card's confirm, which is 3 keys. Jumping back to the breakdown stage is `i`, its row key, Enter, confirm, which is 4. In the inline layout at 80x24, accepting the second pending diff is `d`, its row key, `y`, which is 3. Pairing a phone is `t`, the Pair row key, then the press. A key counter that starts at pane focus with no list open records more than 2 for each of these.
findings.proposed_fix: Count keys from pane focus with no list pre-opened, and assert that in main_flows_within_two_keys. To meet it: (a) in lists whose rows have one obvious action (stages, lenses, projects, the remote list), let the row key act as well as select, so `i 7` runs that stage; (b) replace the per-run cost card with one batched consent per session or plan ('Draft plan stages with Claude, about 4,500 tokens each?'), after which a stage runs with no confirm; (c) in the compact layout, keep the top pending diff line visible with its row key.

findings.title: Bare-digit band hotkeys take over any message that starts with 1, 2 or 3
findings.claim: The band is always shown and owns hotkeys 1 to 3. A bare digit at an empty prompt presses a band Button, so any chat message that starts with 1, 2 or 3 (a numbered list, '2 tests fail', '3 options') runs a Planroom action and loses its first character. The 10 s undo and the toast limit the harm, but the person still has to notice and repair both the action and their message. KICKOFF doesn't require one keystroke from the prompt; it measures from pane focus. So the design takes on this hazard without needing to.
findings.evidence: mod-spike.md: 'A bare digit at the empty prompt presses the mod's band Button (1 pressed band-review)'. architecture.md:1269: 'A bare digit at the empty prompt presses it ... so a digit that started a message costs one keystroke to take back'. mod-api.md:156: in the platform's own words this is a mechanism for a transient survey band. mod-api.md:157: 'Button action: "<engine action>" lets the person's own chord for an engine keybinding press the button from the prompt'. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Never lose or overwrite what someone did' and 'Interrupt a person only for decisions only they can make'. KICKOFF S9 counts keys 'from pane focus'.
findings.failure_scenario: The person types '1. rename cart to basket\n2. ...' into an empty prompt. The `1` accepts Claude's pending batch, the prompt now reads '. rename cart to basket', and a toast flashes. If they then type `1` again to fix the text, that presses the band's primary, which is now the undo. Typing '21 retries is too many' presses the alternative and then undoes it, and the message becomes 'retries is too many'. This happens every session, because the band is always there.
findings.proposed_fix: Don't give the band bare-digit hotkeys. Bind the band's primary to an engine keybinding through Button `action` (mod-api §157), so the person's own chord presses it from the prompt, or reach the band with ctrl+x tab and then a digit (2 keys, still inside S9's bar, which counts from pane focus). If WS5 shows the platform both inserts the digit and presses the button, document that. Add keys.test.tsx::a_message_starting_with_a_digit_reaches_the_composer_unchanged.

findings.title: /room isn't registered as immediate, so pane focus waits for the model's turn to end
findings.claim: The only way to focus the pane is typing /room. A command registered without `immediate: true` runs only after the current turn ends. During a long model turn, which is exactly when the person wants to answer a card that just appeared or reject a ghost, the pane can't be focused. The architecture also lists '/room opening while remote mode is on' as a sync trigger. If bare /room starts the model-driven ArtifactData sync, the most common entry point costs a model turn and a permission prompt every time.
findings.evidence: mod-api.md §3 CommandSpec: 'immediate?: true // runs mid-turn instead of waiting for the turn to end'. architecture.md:1237 and 1271 register `room` with no immediate flag; a grep for 'immediate' finds only SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE. mod-spike.md: 'ctrl+x tab focuses the band, not the pane'. architecture.md:1351: 'Triggers: /room sync; /room opening while remote mode is on'. architecture.md:1352: the mod 'never auto-allows' ArtifactData.
findings.failure_scenario: The chat model is in the middle of a multi-tool turn that drafts the S3 breakdown. The person types /room to accept the first ghosts; nothing happens until the turn ends. With remote mode on, every /room to focus the pane also asks the model to run ArtifactData list, which shows a permission prompt.
findings.proposed_fix: Register `room` with `immediate: true`, and spike in WS5 that bare /room focuses the pane mid-turn. Remove bare /room from the sync triggers and keep the sync on /room sync, `t`, Send to Claude and the stale-sync hint.

findings.title: The unpaired-device card pre-selects No and never says what happens to the person's own phone edits
findings.claim: For KICKOFF's single user, every phone edit made before pairing, or after the page's localStorage loses the pairing key, ends up on one card with No pre-selected. The design never says what No does to those rows: kept, refused and deleted from the inbox, or recoverable. Inbox rows are 'deleted after import'. A band digit can press a card's pre-selected choice, so a stray digit could drop the person's own work.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1346 and contracts.md:939: 'one card ... with No pre-selected'. contracts.md Artifact db table: `inbox/<uid>/events/<docId>` 'deleted after import'. DR-67: the key is kept 'in localStorage'. The Artifact tool contract says browser storage 'can come back empty, or the accessor can throw ... never for state that must persist reliably'. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Never lose or overwrite what someone did' and 'Everything is reversible'.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner renames three blocks on their phone. The Claude app's webview has cleared storage, so the rows go unsigned. At the desk the band's primary is the top card's pre-selected No, and the owner presses 1 at an empty prompt. The rows are acked refused and deleted, the phone shows them as refused, and the renames are gone with no undo path described.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify that No keeps the rows in the store as a dismissed batch that `edit undo` (or reopening the card) can still apply, and that the page shows them as 'not applied, still saved'. Keep cards whose pre-selected choice discards a person's input off the band primary. On load, the page checks that the pairing key exists and, if not, shows 'This device isn't paired' as its face-up Decisions card with the steps to pair.

findings.title: Pairing, Ask Claude and the needs-login state have no place among the five concepts
findings.claim: The canvas's Pair button, the Artifact page's pairing-code entry, the Artifact's Ask Claude button and the tab's needs-login state are top-level UI with no data-concept assigned. S15's exactly_five_concepts asserts that every top-level control carries one of the five ideas, so these will either fail the test or get tagged arbitrarily during the build.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1354: 'The Pair row in the pane's remote list, or the canvas's Pair button' and 'The owner types the code into the Artifact page once'. architecture.md:1353: 'Ask Claude ... only on an explicit tap'. architecture.md:1300-1305 assign places only to the zoom rail, breadcrumb, lens switcher, project shelf, plan board, diff tray, card stack and the action tray or popover (DR-68). feature_list S15: 'data-concept audit on every top-level control'. KICKOFF R14 and S15.
findings.failure_scenario: In M5 a track adds a Pair button to the canvas header and a code field to the Artifact. exactly_five_concepts flags both as untagged, and the track either tags them `decisions` without a design or adds a sixth Setup area.
findings.proposed_fix: Write the placements into design-language.md. An unpaired Artifact device gets a 'Pair this device' Decisions card holding the code field. The canvas's Pair is a choice on that same card, shown when remote mode is on. Ask Claude is a choice on a block's evidence sheet (Levels) or on a card (Decisions). The needs-login state is a full-page empty state, not a control. Extend exactly_five_concepts to cover the pairing and Ask Claude states.

findings.title: The pane has no keys for R6 hand edits, and all 36 hotkeys are already taken
findings.claim: S4 step 1 ('Regroup two components, and change the intended architecture') and R6's rename, re-scope, re-wire and hide have no pane action. The key map uses all 20 free letters plus 1 to 4 for actions and the remaining 12 keys as row keys, so nothing is left for group, move, rename, relate, forbid, hide or pin. In the mod these edits can only be done by typing `/room edit group <stable IDs>` or by asking the chat model and accepting its ghost.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1255-1262 list the action keys z x l p 1-4 a o i d y n f w m s h g u e c t. architecture.md:1268: row keys `5`-`9`, `0`, `b j k q r v`, and 'With the 24 action keys that makes 36 one-key actions, the cap per pane'. mod-api.md:158: 'at most 36 one-key actions per pane'. design-language.md 'Edit by hand' defines these edits for the canvas only. KICKOFF S9: 'every main flow can be driven from the mod'. KICKOFF R13: 'keyboard-first'.
findings.failure_scenario: In the S9 live run the person regroups cart and checkout from the pane. With no key for it, they type /room edit group storefront:component:cart storefront:component:checkout ... with typeahead, or ask Claude and press `a`. The flow can be driven, but it costs dozens of keystrokes or a model turn.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `o` (open detail) on a selected map row show that block's action tray as list rows with row keys (rename, group with, move into, hide, pin, relate to, forbid), each running one `edit` leaf. Target pickers reuse the list. Move curate (`c`) and remote (`t`) into the `o` tray or /room if a letter is needed. Count the S4 regroup in main_flows_within_two_keys.

findings.title: The palette has no tokens for lens yarn colors or block borders, so the contrast test can't check the marks that count
findings.claim: Lenses are 'colored yarn ... one color per relationship kind' and blocks rely on 'a darker shade' border, yet neither has a CSS-variable token. That leaves about ten lens colors (more with `--lens all`) and every block border outside the cohesive palette and outside contrast_meets_the_bar. The block fill tokens measure well below 3:1 on the light felt, so the untested borders are what makes blocks readable.
findings.evidence: design-language.md:12: 'Colored yarn strung between pegs, one color per relationship kind ... Edge color and style per lens'. design-language.md:21-34: the palette lists only block fills and semantic tokens. design-language.md:36: 'the border is the mark that counts'. Computed WCAG ratios on --table #cfe6dc: sunflower #f2b632 1.39:1, sage #6b8f71 2.76:1, tomato #e8492b 2.95:1. KICKOFF look and feel: 'A cohesive palette as CSS variables'. KICKOFF S13 and the design's 3:1 bar for marks.
findings.failure_scenario: A track picks ten edge colors in MapView to separate lenses. Several sit near sage or sunflower and drop below 3:1 on the mint felt. tokens.test.ts passes because those colors aren't tokens, and axe doesn't check SVG edge contrast.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `--yarn-<lens>` tokens (with line styles, so color isn't the only signal) and `--block-*-border` tokens in both themes to packages/ui, and extend contrast_meets_the_bar to include them as marks. Have the lens loader require each lens to map to one of a fixed set of yarn tokens.

findings.title: CLI help adds a sixth 'Setup' group and shows plumbing commands to people
findings.claim: `planroom --help` groups commands by the five ideas plus 'Setup'. Setup holds `serve`, `watch`, `export`, `schema`, `person init`, `import`, `pack` and `doctor`, which are plumbing for the mod, agents and the harness. R14 asks that 'everything else stays internal', so a person reading help meets a sixth bucket and about a dozen commands they never need to run.
findings.evidence: DR-22: 'CLI help groups commands by the five ideas plus "Setup"'. architecture.md:1194-1200 tag scan, share, import, pack, person, open, serve, watch, export, schema, doctor and version as `Setup`. KICKOFF R14: 'The whole mental model a person needs is five ideas ... Everything else stays internal. Before adding a concept, flag or setting, check whether a better default would remove the need for it.' KICKOFF S15: help is snapshot-tested.
findings.failure_scenario: A new user runs `planroom --help` and sees six headings, including `watch --since SEQ --session ID`, `person init` and `schema --commands`. The tiny surface R14 promises doesn't hold at the one CLI entry point, and the help snapshot pins that in.
findings.proposed_fix: Hide plumbing leaves (`watch`, `serve`, `person`, `import`, `export`, `schema`) from human help with clap's `hide`. They stay in `schema --commands --json` and the agent skills. Fold `scan` and `open` under Levels and `share` under Diffs or Decisions. Put the rest behind one line, 'planroom help --all for maintenance commands', and snapshot the five-group help.

verdicts.reason: The loop is real. A cloud session is a container host, so `open` returns opened:false with /room share as its next action. The Artifact's only fallback for views it can't serve tells the person to run /room open, and the design never makes that state depend on the host. Leaving PathView, hunks and other lenses out of the snapshot was a deliberate DR-56 tradeoff. But DR-56 rejected an inbox `ask` on the grounds that 'the empty state already names what to do', and on exactly the hosts where the Artifact is the only canvas, what it names leads back to itself. On the surface R13 provides for 'when localhost isn't reachable', that breaks principle 1 (understanding and control at a fraction of the effort, a working next action instead of a dead end). R2 questions are still reachable through chat and the pane, which lowers the user impact somewhat. Still, the canvas surface on that host has no working route to Lenses or PathView, and its next action is circular. I couldn't refute it, so I'm upholding it.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1316: 'On the Artifact, PathView, Anatomy, the impact heat ramp, evidence text, diff hunks, other lenses and intent next render ... "Needs your computer: open this view there with /room open"'. architecture.md:1198 and DR-29 round 2: 'Where no browser can be seen (... a container host, ...) opens nothing and returns opened: false with an empty state whose next action is /room share'. architecture.md:503 lists CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE as a supported temporary host. contracts.md:919 has a single static `unavailable: Empty`, with no host-dependent variant. DR-56's rejected alternative relies on 'the empty state already names what to do'. KICKOFF R13: the canvas is 'also published as a Claude Artifact for when localhost isn't reachable'.

verdicts.reason: The pane's only lens and project controls are `l` 'next lens' and `p` 'next project', and no lens or project list is defined anywhere (I grepped every doc under review). With 10 lenses, reaching a given one can take up to 9 presses from pane focus. KICKOFF S9 (tier B) says 'Every action is at most two keystrokes from pane focus'. The design reads S9 as counting pane presses after /room ('any pane action then takes at most two keys'), and lens choice breaks that. A different reading of S9 would count the whole typed `/room map --lens X` as one entry point, but the design doesn't rely on that reading, and its own key-count test wouldn't exercise it. Because this would make a tier B assertion fail, it's material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1255: '`z` up a level, `x` down, `l` next lens, `p` next project'. architecture.md:1270: '/room focuses the pane, and any pane action then takes at most two keys'. A grep for 'lens list' or 'project list' finds nothing in the docs. feature_list.json S9 assert: 'every action in the scripted flows is at most two real key presses from pane focus'. KICKOFF S9.

verdicts.reason: Row keys only select rows the person can already see, and the list area holds 'the list the last key opened'. So a row behind `i`, `f`, `w`, `t`, or `d` in the compact layout needs a list key, a row key and an action key. Runs that spend also need the cost card's 'second, deliberate key'. For the first stage that's i, Enter, confirm (3 keys); for any other stage it's i, row key, Enter, confirm (4). The feature_list assertion 'Enter on a stage row under i runs intent next --stage S through its cost card, within two keys from pane focus' can't hold if the cost card's confirm counts. And the S9 assertion is limited to 'any visible row', which hides the shortfall. Nothing in the docs pre-opens the list the next action needs. Upheld as material against S9's tier B bar.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1257: '`i` intent: the stages, then lint findings, as list rows; `Enter` on a stage runs it'. architecture.md:1262: 'the list the last key opened'. architecture.md:1268: 'A row key selects its row, and an action key then acts on the selected row ... So acting on any visible row takes at most two keys'. architecture.md:1269: 'drafting a plan stage, shows on the band as a label that opens its card in the pane, where confirming takes a second, deliberate key'. architecture.md:1266: in the compact layout, 'Diffs, drift, who and the mini-map move behind their keys (d, f, w, m)'. feature_list.json S9 asserts.

verdicts.reason: The hazard is real. The platform consumes a bare digit at an empty composer ('never the composer, save that a bare digit in an empty one answers a band Button'), so a message that starts with 1 to 3 loses that character and presses a band action. But the design limits the harm on purpose. Band actions can only name leaves that can be undone, can't spend and aren't hand-offs. The pack loader enforces that rule. Each press shows a toast, and for 10 s the band's primary is the undo. So nothing irreversible, paid or repo-changing can come from a stray digit, and principle 1's 'everything is reversible' holds. What's left is having to retype a character and occasionally undo. That won't fail any tier A or B scenario, and it isn't a real data-loss or security risk. DR-54 weighed a confirm on every band press and rejected it. So this is minor.
verdicts.evidence: mod-api.md (Keyboard and focus): Button hotkey 'never the composer, save that a bare digit in an empty one answers a band Button'. architecture.md:1269: the band names 'only commands whose undo class isn't NotUndoable, whose permission class isn't handoff, and that can't spend ... The pack loader refuses a [[suggestions]] entry whose action breaks this rule ... For the next 10 s the band's primary Button is that edit undo'. DR-54, alternatives rejected: 'A confirmation on every band press: it costs a key on the common, reversible case'. feature_list S9 asserts band_next_is_undoable and the toast plus undo.

verdicts.reason: This is real and correctly rated minor. mod-api research recommends `immediate: true` so /room can run mid-turn, but the architecture registers `room` without it. A grep for 'immediate' in the architecture docs finds only SQLite IMMEDIATE transactions. Bare /room opening is also listed as a sync trigger while remote mode is on, so the common way into the pane can kick off a model-driven ArtifactData call that goes through the normal permission flow. Nothing in the docs handles either point.
verdicts.evidence: mod-api.md:201: 'immediate?: true // runs mid-turn instead of waiting for the turn to end'. mod-api.md:400: '`immediate: true` lets `/room focus` and `/room decide` run mid-turn'. architecture.md:1271 (/room family) has no immediate flag. architecture.md:1351: 'Triggers: /room sync; /room opening while remote mode is on'. DR-31 (decisions.md:608): 'Sync runs on /room sync, /room opening, ...'. architecture.md:1352: 'never auto-allows it through tool.check'.

verdicts.reason: This is real and minor.
